_comment: The one contrast gate a dashboard palette clears (fill step 15). Consumed by frontend/src/composition/paletteContrast.ts (paletteVerdict) and pinned against backend/app/display/palette_contrast.py (palette_verdict) by backend/tests/test_palette_contrast.py and frontend/src/composition/paletteContrast.test.ts, which both run every case below. The palette is the look's tokens (library/definitions/themes.json) with the override merged over them; every colour must be #rrggbb (either case) or the palette is invalid. Pairs are judged in order and the first that falls below `required` is the verdict. Contrast is WCAG 2.x: each sRGB byte b/255 is linearised (c <= 0.04045 ? c/12.92 : ((c+0.055)/1.055)^2.4), luminance is 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B, and the ratio is (lighter + 0.05)/(darker + 0.05). `scrim` is the worst-case backdrop text reads over a picture: the palette is light-text when luminance(text) > luminance(background); the caption grey g is the inverse-linearised luminance of captionSurface as a continuous 0-255 value (l <= 0.0031308 ? 12.92l : 1.055 l^(1/2.4) - 0.055, times 255, l clamped to [0,1]); the raw alpha is 1 - g/255 for light text (a black scrim over a white pixel) and g/255 otherwise (a white scrim over a black pixel); alpha is rounded UP to two places (ceil(raw*100)/100); the scrim is the grey byte round-half-up(scrimByte*alpha + pixel*(1-alpha)), clamped to 0..255, with scrimByte 0 and pixel 255 for light text and scrimByte 255 and pixel 0 otherwise. A verdict's ratio is rounded DOWN to two places; Studio prints it rounded down to one ('Text on Background is 1.6:1; it needs 4.5:1'). A case's `scrim` pins the composited backdrop; `verdict` is null when every pair clears.
